source: Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud Root Cause Analysis? (2026)
finding: Full OpenRCA run on 5 LLMs. The best model finds the exact root cause (component, time and reason all right) in only 12.5% of incidents.
numbers: 1,675 agent runs; 335 incidents; perfect detection 3.9% to 12.5% across 5 models (Gemini 2.5 Pro best at 12.5%).
limits: Semi-automated failure labelling with human check; mitigation tested only on a Bank subset (70 tasks).
agent_relevance: Diagnosis by LLM agents is weak even with strong models. Treat any single-pass diagnosis as low trust.

source: Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud RCA? (failure taxonomy, 2026)
finding: Two failures dominate every model: hallucinated interpretation of retrieved data, and incomplete exploration. The model reaches the right data and then tells a story the data does not support.
numbers: Hallucination in Interpretation 1193/1675 runs (71.2%); Incomplete Exploration 1071 (63.9%); Symptom-as-Cause 669 (39.9%, 68.4% for Gemini 2.5 Pro); No Cross-Validation 311 (18.6%).
limits: Pitfalls overlap, so percentages sum above 100%. One Controller plus Executor framework only.
agent_relevance: Symptom-as-Cause and No Cross-Validation are the abductive errors: take the first anomaly as the cause. A code check that each candidate is tested against all observations answers this.

source: Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud RCA? (mitigation, 2026)
finding: Prompt-only fixes failed. Hypothesis-driven prompting widened exploration but did not cut hallucinated interpretation. Pitfall-aware prompting was acknowledged in traces and ignored in practice. Showing the Controller the Executor's code and raw errors cut communication pitfalls by about 14 to 15 points.
numbers: Claude Sonnet 4, 70 Bank tasks. Enriched protocol: perfect detections GPT-5 mini 0 to 2 (0.0 to 4.9%), Gemini 2.5 Pro 1 to 3 (2.4 to 7.3%); steps -22.1% (11.9 to 9.2); time -22.3%; tokens per step +24.8%.
limits: Tiny absolute counts (2 to 3 cases of 41). Bank domain only.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: show real output, not summaries. Telling the model to hypothesise more is not enough; structure must change.

source: Stalled, Biased, and Confused: Reasoning Failures in LLMs for Cloud-Based RCA (2026)
finding: Controlled test of six open LLMs on RCA with a plain one-shot prompt (Straight-Shot), ReAct and Plan-and-Execute. Agentic loops often gave no gain and for small models made things worse, sometimes below random guessing.
numbers: 48,000 simulated failures, 228 days compute, 2 datasets (GAIA, OpenRCA-based). Llama 3.2 3B location accuracy @3 fell from 0.31 (Straight-Shot) to 0.23 (ReAct) to 0.05 (Plan-and-Execute). Qwen3 32B best hypothesis accuracy @3: 0.36 on set A, 0.09 on set B (larger hypothesis space).
limits: Open models only (3B to 104B); simulated failures; LLM-as-judge labels on 3,073 of 19,200 traces.
agent_relevance: More scaffold is not better. Gain depends on model capacity; for weak models structure amplifies errors. Test the loop against a plain baseline.

source: Stalled, Biased, and Confused (reasoning failure predictors, 2026)
finding: Anchoring, stalled repetition, arbitrary evidence selection and failure to update belief predict wrong diagnoses. These are the abductive failure modes (fixing on one hypothesis). For strong models, agentic exploration improved propagation-path validity.
numbers: RF-13 anchoring, RF-12 repetition, RF-07 arbitrary evidence selection, RF-09 failure to update belief: each at least 15% drop in correctness (risk difference below -0.15) and correct answer at least 45% less likely (risk ratio below 0.55). 16-item failure taxonomy. Llama 3.3 path accuracy @3 0.61 (Straight-Shot) to 0.73 (ReAct) to 0.78 (Plan-and-Execute) on set A.
limits: Associational, not causal; judge is an LLM.
agent_relevance: Gives a concrete detector list for the impasse signal: repetition, one hypothesis kept after contrary evidence, evidence picked without a rule.

source: Exploring LLM-based Agents for Root Cause Analysis (2024)
finding: A ReAct agent with retrieval tools matched retrieval and chain-of-thought baselines on correctness but hallucinated far less. Adding discussion comments from past incidents did not help.
numbers: Manual labelling of 100 predictions per model: correct 35% (ReAct) vs 39% (baselines); hallucination 4% (ReAct) vs 12% (CoT) vs 40% (retrieval baseline k=10). Of the retrieval baseline's wrong answers 49% (29/59) were hallucinations, vs 18% (11/59) for CoT and 6% (4/63) for ReAct.
limits: One company's production incidents, GPT-4 family, small manual sample.
agent_relevance: Looking up facts instead of recalling them cuts invented causes. Argues for evidence-gathering steps before naming a cause.

source: RCAgent: Cloud Root Cause Analysis by Autonomous Agents with Tool-Augmented LLMs (2023)
finding: Industrial RCA agent (Flink jobs) beats plain ReAct by adding observation compression, trajectory-level self-consistency and a stability fix. Without the observation compression module the agent breaks down.
numbers: Reported full pass rate 99.38% within 15 steps, invalid rate 7.93%. Removing the observation key-snippet module cut pass rate by 33.54% with a 70.95% invalid rate.
limits: Numbers taken from text extraction of tables, partly unclear; in-house data; text-similarity metrics.
agent_relevance: Self-consistency over whole trajectories is used in practice; per G4 agreement stays a hint only.

source: OpenRCA: Can LLMs Locate the Root Cause of Software Failures? (2025, ICLR)
finding: Reference benchmark for LLM RCA on real telemetry from three enterprise systems. Known here only through citing papers (c01, c09).
numbers: Best prior baseline 15.2% correct per the EviRCA comparison; 12.5% perfect detection per c01.
limits: Original not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Use these numbers as a floor for unscaffolded abduction on real systems.

source: EviRCA: Decoupling Evidence Extraction from Reasoning for Microservice RCA (2026)
finding: Deterministic code builds compact evidence cards; the LLM reasons only over those through read-only tools. Accuracy on OpenRCA about tripled. The remaining bottleneck is judging the evidence, not finding it.
numbers: OpenRCA correct rate 40.6% (qwen3.7-plus) and 43.9% (deepseek-v4-pro) vs best baseline 15.2%; tokens down 15 to 26 times; time down 3 to 20 times; hard multi-factor cases previously near zero now solved.
limits: Authors' own system and comparison; OpenRCA only; not an independent replication.
agent_relevance: Direct support for the code-computes, model-ranks split (G5).

source: OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision (PAVE, 2026)
finding: Scoring only the final answer hides ungrounded diagnoses. With labelled causal paths, agents often name a right service but cannot show the path from cause to symptom.
numbers: 500 instances, 3 microservice systems, 11 frontier LLMs: exact root-cause set 20.7%; pair F1 34.1%; any correct service 76.0%; grounded in verified path 61.5%; Node F1 62.2% vs Edge F1 43.4% (gap 18.8 points).
limits: Fault-injection systems, not production; labels built by forward intervention.
agent_relevance: The model finds the suspect but not the mechanism. Require a forward check (predict the symptoms from the cause) before accepting a diagnosis.

source: How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data? (2026)
finding: Evidence computed once offline and given identically to all arms. Rules mined from past audit reports raised score on a held-out cloudbed; removing the written procedure did not hurt.
numbers: Full Score 14.10 to 35.90 with mined rules vs 24.36 manual rules vs 19.23 label-and-schema control. Removing the 5-step procedure raised Full Score in all three conditions, none surviving multiple-testing correction.
limits: Abstract only read. Label-supervised mining; OpenRCA-specific.
agent_relevance: A fixed diagnostic procedure may not beat plain evidence plus learned rules. Weak support for caution about long scripts.

source: Rethinking Tool Design for Agentic RCA: A Controlled Empirical Study (2026)
finding: More structured diagnosis tools did not always help. Free Python matched or beat the top tool level, extra tools sometimes lowered localisation, and agents overrode correct tool recommendations after seeing more evidence.
numbers: 375 failure cases, 3 systems, Qwen3.7-Plus: top-1 localisation 85.4% (free Python L0) vs 82.8% (full diagnosis tools L3) at under half the time; accuracy 52.7% (L1) to 68.8% (L2) to 82.8% (L3); adding L3 hurt Qwen3-8B, which rarely invokes it.
limits: Qwen models only; partly read.
agent_relevance: A model can talk itself out of a correct computed diagnosis. Code-decided acceptance (G5) matters.

source: LLMs Can See the Smoke but not the Fire: Evaluating Abductive Reasoning with Elenchos (2026)
finding: Abduction as an inverse problem: given a reference rule system (lambda-calculus kernel) and a possibly mutated copy, say whether it changed and which rules. Models detect change far better than they name the cause. This is simulate-and-compare diagnosis.
numbers: 13 LLMs: kernel detection 0.65 vs exact mutation attribution 0.28 (over k=1,2 and prompt levels). Hardest setting (minimal prompt plus interacting mutations) mean accuracy 0.02. In 86.5% of detect-but-misattribute cases the probe budget (Pmax 50) was unused. A scripted reflex agent using the example probes was perfect at k=1 additive; no LLM wrote equivalent probes alone.
limits: Synthetic formal system; the reasoning-budget finding is flagged by the authors as needing validation.
agent_relevance: LLMs stop before using their probe budget. Code should force discriminating probes (O7) and compare against the reference model.

source: Elenchos (2026): interacting faults and prompt scaffolding
finding: Interacting multiple faults break diagnosis, the multiple-fault case classic model-based diagnosis handles with hitting sets. More structure in the system prompt gave large gains; weak models failed without it.
numbers: Accuracy falls with less prompt information (Level 0 best), higher mutation count k, and interaction; some models reach zero accuracy in the no-hint interacting setting; extra inference-time reasoning gave only modest gains.
limits: Preliminary on reasoning budget; one task family.
agent_relevance: Expect single-fault bias: the agent finds one cause and stops. Enumerate multi-fault candidates by code.

source: Don't Let Me Ask for It: LLMs in Active Multi-Turn Information Acquisition for Abductive Inference (Alien Abduction game, 2026)
finding: Hidden-function discovery game. Evidence given upfront beats evidence spread over turns, and oracle-chosen examples beat the model's own queries. Models fit hypotheses to evidence they chose themselves without separating them from rivals.
numbers: 4 models, 50 target functions in 5 domains, 15-turn budget. Overall success GPT5.4 0.64, Mistral-Large-3 0.20, Qwen3.6-35B 0.03 (parser errors in 40.64% of Qwen instances; Qwen and Mistral burn all turns without converging). Passive-output success GPT5.4 0.78 vs GPT5.4-mini 0.40. Non-commitment hit 45.2% of Mistral and 40.6% of Qwen turns vs 4.6% for GPT5.4.
limits: Primitive Python functions; GPT5.4 also generated the targets, a possible home advantage.
agent_relevance: Self-chosen tests confirm the current guess. Choose tests by code for separating rivals, not by the model.

source: Thinking effort aligns between humans and reasoning models in abductive reasoning (2026)
finding: On abductive story items (pick which of two hypotheses explains both observations), the reasoning length of large reasoning models tracks human reaction time, and models and humans fail on the same items.
numbers: N=120 humans, 160 items; 9 models. Partial r (reasoning tokens vs human RT, length controlled): GPT-OSS-120B 0.552, GPT-OSS-20B 0.41, Qwen3-235B 0.359, DeepSeek-R1 0.327, Kimi-K2 0.303, GLM-4.5-Air 0.263, Qwen3-32B 0.229, DeepSeek-V3 (non-reasoning) 0.197. R1 vs V3 not significant (Fisher z 1.23, p .217). Human accuracy 78.8%; on items R1 got right humans scored 82.5%, wrong 47.8%; model-consensus vs human accuracy r=0.668. Multi-run sampling raised GPT-OSS-20B from 0.41 to 0.55; temperature 2 hurt.
limits: Short two-choice narrative items (Peirce-style abduction), not diagnosis.
agent_relevance: Reasoning length is a usable difficulty signal, so an impasse detector can use token count. Shared errors with humans mean shared blind spots (G4).

source: Abductive Commonsense Reasoning (Bhagavatula et al., 2019)
finding: Introduced the alphaNLI and alphaNLG two-observation abduction tasks that later LLM studies such as c16 reuse in similar form.
numbers: Not opened beyond the title page.
limits: Title page only.
agent_relevance: Background for the item format.

source: True Detective: A Deep Abductive Reasoning Benchmark Undoable for GPT-3 and Challenging for GPT-4 (2022)
finding: Long detective puzzles (5 Minute Mystery) where models do poorly. Chain of thought helps the stronger model; supplying the correct reasoning chain lifts it to near best-human level, so the weakness is generating the explanation, not applying it.
numbers: 4 to 5 answer options, random 0.24; humans average 47% (first tries, about 2000 attempts per puzzle), top humans over 80%. GPT-3.5 0.28, GPT-4 vanilla 0.27, GPT-4 with chain of thought 0.38. With golden chain of thought GPT-3.5 reaches 0.63 and GPT-4 0.83.
limits: 2022-era models only; public website puzzles may be in training data.
agent_relevance: Building the explanation chain is the bottleneck; a good chain nearly solves it. Case for explicit hypothesis generation with outside checking.

source: Towards Accurate Differential Diagnosis with Large Language Models (2023)
finding: A medically tuned LLM produced differentials for hard NEJM cases. Alone it beat unassisted clinicians on the list, and it raised clinicians' own lists when they used it.
numbers: 302 NEJM cases, 20 clinicians. Model alone top-1 29.2%, top-10 59.1% vs clinicians unassisted top-10 33.6% (p=0.04). With search 44.5%; with LLM 51.8% (vs 36.1% without help, McNemar 45.7, p<0.01). Top-1 with LLM 25.2% vs 15.9% unassisted.
limits: Public case reports, possible contamination; written cases, not real clinic flow.
agent_relevance: Generate-many-then-rank gives a real gain. Top-1 near 29% shows ranking still needs checks.

source: Auditing evaluation artifacts and data leakage in LLM systems for rare disease diagnosis (2026)
finding: A reconstructed agentic diagnosis system lost much of its accuracy once candidate-space contamination was removed. Reported gains partly come from leakage.
numbers: 60,000+ cases. Cross-dataset mean Recall@1 fell from 54.3% to 40.3% (Hedges g 0.94). Supervised classifiers fell from 42.9% to 16.7% on external cohorts (Cohen d 2.01).
limits: Rare disease domain; one reconstructed framework.
agent_relevance: Failed-replication style warning: LLM diagnosis scores can be inflated. Keep held-out tests (G3).

source: Ontology-guided multi-agent reasoning for explainable differential diagnosis (MedMAS-DDx, 2026)
finding: Neuro-symbolic diagnosis: LLMs only extract symptoms and ask questions; deterministic code scores and ranks diseases against an ontology. Follow-up questions target the most discriminating missing symptom.
numbers: Q4DX benchmark, 198 variant cases (99 at 80% and 99 at 50% symptom disclosure), 29 diagnoses. Top-1 18.7% (37/198) before questions to 21.2% (42/198) after; top-3 25.8% to 27.3%. Cited baseline accuracy falls from 51% to 44% to 37% as disclosure falls from 100 to 80 to 50%. Only 6 of 42 correct top-1 were exact string matches.
limits: Low absolute accuracy; small gains not tested for significance; semantic match threshold 0.6.
agent_relevance: A working LLM loop with abduction plus discriminating questions and code scoring. Gain is small, so do not oversell.

source: Agentic4PDM: Host-Governed Evidence Admissibility for Industrial Fault Diagnosis (2026)
finding: Sensor fault diagnosis where agents compare each signal with labelled references of every candidate class and propose follow-up measurements, while a deterministic host controls which evidence counts.
numbers: Macro F1 +7.5% over the strongest baseline on the GRS set and over +12% on the hard baseline-failure and industrial sets; agentic baselines ZARA and FETA fell behind time-series foundation models.
limits: Margins read from text and figures; customer data not public.
agent_relevance: Another working case of the split: model proposes tests, code gates evidence.

source: Before the Arrest: Benchmarking LLMs on Criminal Profiling from Incomplete Evidence (2026)
finding: Abductive profiling from scene evidence is the hardest of three tasks. Models fall behind human experts and show gender, age and motive bias.
numbers: 2,500 real homicide cases, 5 countries, 9 LLMs. Inferential categories (motive, victim-offender relationship) are the bottleneck; model scores on profiling items mostly in the 40s to 50s (F1 percent); one expert category scored 90.73% F1.
limits: Table reading was partial; labels are case records.
agent_relevance: Abduction with missing facts invites stereotype fill-in. Mark attributes unknown instead of guessing.

source: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis (DRAGO, 2026)
finding: An LLM critique of its own output damages good answers. Deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis plus a rule to keep a rewrite only if diagnosed error weight strictly falls cuts that damage.
numbers: Regressions on initially correct specs 11.8% (LLM-diagnostic repair) vs 1.3% (DRAGO). Accuracy +12.9 points over zero-shot and +8.7 over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged over 5 benchmarks (SMT-LIB2, MiniZinc, PDDL) and 4 models. 50% (3,086) of the Planetarium floor-tile split was inconsistent with references.
limits: Needs formalism-specific diagnostic rules; formal domains only.
agent_relevance: Quantified support for G2 and G5: ungrounded critique flips 11.8% of right answers to wrong; evidence-gated acceptance prevents it.

source: One Hypothesis Is Not Enough: Abductive Reasoning with Agentic Hypothesis Refinement over Knowledge Graphs (HypoAgent, 2026)
finding: Closing the abductive loop (propose, execute, find which branch fails to cover observations, revise) beats one-shot hypothesis generation over knowledge graphs.
numbers: Unconditional DBpedia50: Jaccard 0.8653 to 0.8746 across LLM backends vs 0.6276 (AbductiveKGR) and 0.6900 (DARK). Adding earlier hypotheses as reference raised BioKG Jaccard 0.892 to 0.910.
limits: Structured logic hypotheses over KGs; a small trained generator does the proposing.
agent_relevance: Fragment-level coverage locates what a failing hypothesis misses, the abductive version of a conflict. A template for the O8 reframe step.

source: Neurosymbolic Clinical Trial Matching via LLM-Driven Abduction and Logical Verification (2026)
finding: LLM proposes missing facts abductively and a logic checker verifies them. Beats standalone LLM and non-abductive neurosymbolic setups.
numbers: Up to 30% relative improvement over zero-shot baselines; complementary with chain of thought.
limits: Abstract only; trial matching, not fault diagnosis.
agent_relevance: LLM as abducer of missing premises, solver as verifier: a pattern to copy.

source: Abductive reasoning and Model-based reasoning (Wikipedia, 2026 read)
finding: Abductive diagnosis in AI: given a theory linking faults to effects and observed effects, derive the fault sets that explain them (T union E entails O, E consistent with T, minimal). Internist-I used abduction for internal medicine. Neither page names Reiter, GDE or the Ab predicate.
numbers: Peirce 1903 form: surprising fact C; if A then C as a matter of course; so suspect A. Set-cover form: find H whose effects cover all manifestations.
limits: Encyclopedia; no replication data; first 100,000 characters read.
agent_relevance: Gives the formal test for a code checker: a candidate must entail every observation and stay consistent with the model.

source: Reiter (1987) A theory of diagnosis from first principles; de Kleer and Williams (1987) Diagnosing multiple faults
finding: Founding works. Reiter defines a diagnosis as a minimal set of components assumed abnormal (Ab) that is consistent with model and observations. GDE adds candidate tracking and probe choice by entropy.
numbers: Not opened this session; from background knowledge.
limits: Memory only.
agent_relevance: Source of the Ab predicate and the multiple-fault idea; see sibling subfield 01 for conflicts.

source: Console and Torasso (1991) A spectrum of logical definitions of model-based diagnosis
finding: Abductive diagnosis (cover every observation) and consistency-based diagnosis (do not contradict) sit on a spectrum; abductive needs fault models, consistency-based needs only normal behaviour.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Memory only.
agent_relevance: With a fault model, use the abductive reading; without one, consistency. Fits the S5 versus S7 choice.
